title: Telegram System Events: The Cross-Platform Reference
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Every system event Telegram can record in a chat, on both iOS and Android, with what each one means, what the clients call it on each platform, and which ones the LEAPPs parsers decode in detail.

title: Telegram on Both Sides: New iOS and Android Coverage in iLEAPP and ALEAPP
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Telegram now has fifteen artifacts across iLEAPP and ALEAPP, covering accounts, chats, contacts, cached profiles, and the app settings that tell you whether media ever touched the device. Here is what we added, what it proves, and the parts we could not validate.

title: Every Step You Take, Eight Years Later: Android UsageStats and Recent Tasks
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Android's pattern-of-life evidence grew from readable XML into tokenized protobufs carrying app lifecycle, lock state, notifications, services, task roots, and more. We went back to the source, updated ALEAPP, and came away with better data—and better warnings about what it actually proves.

title: Apple Unified Log Predicates in iLEAPP: The Reference
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Every Unified Log message predicate iLEAPP searches for, artifact by artifact, with the processes involved, the iOS versions each pattern was observed on, the sources that documented them, and the caveats that keep you honest.

title: Extracting, Processing, and Querying Apple Unified Logs from an iOS Device
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Apple Unified Logs can show locks, app launches, connectivity, navigation, and more. iLEAPP now parses them natively on Windows, Linux, and macOS. No Mac and no JSON conversion required. Here is the updated workflow.

title: Introducing DLEAPP
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The seventh LEAPP is here. DLEAPP parses desktop application artifacts — Discord, Signal, WhatsApp, and Wire so far — and gives a home to any artifact that does not fit the other LEAPPs. Packaged for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

title: Everybody Gets a Release!
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: iLEAPP, ALEAPP, RLEAPP, and VLEAPP are all at v2026.2.0, and LAVA is at v0.14.0. Biome artifacts, iOS 26 photos, AI image provenance, recovered clipboards, a Snapchat overhaul, row tagging in LAVA, and a lot more.

title: Digital Forensics Now Ahora Habla Español
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The Digital Forensics Now podcast now has a Spanish edition, in our own voices, built with open source AI models running locally and verified line by line by a native speaker. Para la comunidad DFIR de habla hispana.

title: ASTC, Cython, and bugs!
author: Bruno Constanzo
excerpt: What do texture decompression, C-extensions for python, and LEAPPs have in common? Read to find out!

title: Feature Highlight: Recent Run History in LAVA
author: James Habben
excerpt: A quick look at the new opt-in LEAPPs recent run history feature and how LAVA can use it to put recent parser outputs right on the welcome screen.

title: A Trip Through the United iOS App
author: James Habben
excerpt: A look at United Airlines iOS app research in iLEAPP, including where the data lived, which rabbit holes mattered, and why nearby app/plugin data can change the shape of the parser.

title: Be Careful What You Wish For
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The genie can grant almost anything. It cannot grant you judgment. And judgment is the one thing you need in order to control it.

title: Spotting AI Generated Images in iLEAPP and ALEAPP
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: iLEAPP and ALEAPP can now flag AI generated images by reading content provenance two ways, C2PA Content Credentials manifests and the IPTC Digital Source Type in XMP. Pure Python, no new dependencies, and usable today straight from the source.

title: The Rules Keep Changing
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The first fully LLM-generated set of artifacts lands in iLEAPP: fourteen Biome parsers built from public community research and test data, 3,668 rows of previously unparsed data on the first clean pass. If coding is now accessible to everyone, what does that mean for tooling in digital forensics?

title: The Apps We Are Not Parsing (Yet)
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Batch LEAPP now answers a question I have wanted answered for years. Out of all the apps installed on our test devices, which ones do the LEAPPs actually parse, and which ones are we missing? One flag, one database, and a data-driven module-writing roadmap.

title: SELECT * FROM life360 WHERE alibi = FALSE;
author: Heather Charpentier
excerpt: A forensic analysis of the Life360 app on Android — account identifiers, Circle members, saved Places and alerts, pet trackers, drives and driving events, location history, waypoints, and battery levels, all now supported in ALEAPP.

title: Getting It Done with Home Depot iOS Artifacts
author: James Habben
excerpt: A look at new iLEAPP parsing for the Home Depot iOS app, including account details, store preferences, searches, viewed products, shopping lists, cached location, and a few useful cache artifacts.

title: Introducing Batch LEAPP
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: Batch LEAPP runs any LEAPP tool across an entire folder of extractions and builds one report index that links every result, with hashing and a manifest for your case file. Here is what it does and how to get it.

title: Installing LEAPPs and LAVA on macOS with Homebrew
author: James Habben
excerpt: Mac users can install iLEAPP, ALEAPP, RLEAPP, VLEAPP, their GUI apps, and LAVA with a few Homebrew commands from the LEAPPs tap.

title: Decoding Apple ATX Images in iLEAPP
author: James Habben
excerpt: Wallpaper research led to a broader Apple image-cache problem: ATX texture files. Here is how iLEAPP now parses and decodes many of them, with a reusable parser that should be easy to port into other tools.

title: Recovering Pre-iOS 16 Wallpaper from SpringBoard
author: James Habben
excerpt: A quick research note on extracting older iOS wallpaper files from SpringBoard, including legacy cpbitmap conversion and JPG thumbnail handling in iLEAPP.

title: How to Write an iLEAPP Module
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The LEAPPs ecosystem runs on contributions. A module is a single Python file — and this guide walks through everything: module structure, SQLite and plist parsing, timestamp handling, LAVA conversation view, and submitting a pull request.

title: LEAPPing with LAVA
author: Kevin Pagano
excerpt: LAVA is another way to view reports created out of iLEAPP, ALEAPP, RLEAPP, and VLEAPP. Here is a look at the new features that make it stand out from the HTML reporting it is set to replace.

title: Website Update - Search, Better Docs, and More
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The LEAPPs website got a big update. Here is a rundown of everything that changed, from site-wide search to improved docs and a more consistent footer across every page.

title: Introducing the LEAPPs Blog
author: Alexis Brignoni
excerpt: The LEAPPs project now has a blog — a place for artifact deep dives, tool updates, and community write-ups. Here's how it works and how you can contribute.
